Technical education in Japan
abstract: Junior colleges of engineering and technical colleges are the primary sources of engineering technicians in Japan. There are eight junior colleges of engineering which are the junior college division of iiatimal universities and 65 technical colleges. Junior colleges of engineering offer instruction only in the evening with programs which are of three years duration. Technical colleges are five years institutions equivalent to three years at the high school level and two years a t the junior college level. The quality of instruction a t both types of institutions appears to be very good. Students completing the program of instruction a t either type of institutions receives a certificate of capletion as no degree less than a BS degree is awarded in Japan.

Cooperative Learning In Engineering Workshop
abstract: The purpose of this workshop is to introduce Cooperative Learning as an alternative approach to teaching in the Engineering Curriculum. A class is divided into permanent groups for the duration of the course and these become the focus of all student activities. The instructor provides the class with a Lesson Plan which details the objectives and activities for each session. The primary feature of cooperative learning is the interdependence of the students within their groups which leads to the active involvement of all class members. The method has been used in a wide variety of disciplines but only sparingly in Engineering education. There will be two workshops presented at the conference, an introductory session and a more advanced working session.

Civil Engineering Department
abstract: The Department of Civil Engineering at the University of South Carolina, Columbia, SC, USA offers programs of study at both the undergraduate and graduate (Master's and Ph.D.) levels. Students may specialize in the traditional fields of Civil Engineering, including applied mechanics, structures, geotechnical engineering, traffic and transportation, and environmental and water resources engineering. There are fourteen faculty in the Department, actively engaged in teaching, research, and administration. Current faculty research interests and laboratory facilities available to support the experimental programs are described.
